hints: Use section formulae on the position vectors: average the endpoints for a midpoint and divide a line segment in the stated ratio.
Since $BN=2NC$, point $N$ is two-thirds of the way from $B$ to $C$, so use $\overrightarrow{ON}=\overrightarrow{OB}+\tfrac23(\overrightarrow{OC}-\overrightarrow{OB})$.
walkthrough: Use a correct method to find $\overrightarrow{ON}$

hints: A vector line equation needs one point on the line and a direction vector parallel to it.
Use $\overrightarrow{OM}=(2,1,0)$ as the fixed point and form the direction $\overrightarrow{MN}=\overrightarrow{ON}-\overrightarrow{OM}$ from part (a).
Write $\mathbf r=\overrightarrow{OM}+\lambda\overrightarrow{MN}$, noting that any non-zero scalar multiple of the direction is equivalent.
walkthrough: Carry out a correct method to form a vector equation for $MN$
Obtain a correct equation in any form, e.g. $\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\\-1\end{pmatrix}$

ai_rubric.Finding Equations of Straight Lines: Derives an equation, e.g. $\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\\-1\end{pmatrix}$. The final result is $\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\\-1\end{pmatrix}$.

hints: At an intersection, the position vectors given by the line $MN$ and a vector equation for $AB$ are equal.
Form $AB$ as $\mathbf r=(1,0,1)+\mu(-1,5,1)$ and equate it to $(2,1,0)+\lambda(1,-3,-1)$.
Equate corresponding components and solve the simultaneous equations for one parameter, then substitute that parameter into its line equation to obtain $\overrightarrow{OQ}$.
walkthrough: State a correct vector equation for $AB$ in any form, e.g. $\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}-1\\5\\1\end{pmatrix}$
Equate components of $AB$ and $MN$ and solve for $\lambda$ or for $\mu$
Obtain position vector $\begin{pmatrix}-1\\10\\3\end{pmatrix}$, or equivalent, for $Q$

ai_rubric.Vector Line Intersections: Gives a vector equation for $AB$, e.g. $\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}-1\\5\\1\end{pmatrix}$. Equates components of $AB$ and $MN$ and solves for $\lambda$ or for $\mu$. The final result is $\overrightarrow{OQ}=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\10\\3\end{pmatrix}$.
